source_routes.title: User-Centered Redesign of Monitoring Alarms: A Pre–Post Study on Perception, Functionality, and Recognizability Following Real-Life Clinical Implementation
source_routes.reading_extent: Web-rendered public full-article HTML: abstract, Methods §§2.1–2.8, Results §§3.1–3.6, Discussion §4, Conclusions §5; tables were available as HTML text, but original PDF bytes, supplement audio, image-rendered figures and source data not verified

author_reported_not_independently_extrac.study_context: single-centre hospital implementation of revised patient-monitoring alarm sounds; recognition test conducted with laptop and simulated OR noise, not observation of live clinical responses
author_reported_not_independently_extrac.training_preexposure: 34/77 reported attending January 2024 training; authors reported separate sensitivity re-analysis

cautions: Two measurements on the same 77 re-enrolled people are not 154 independent participants; 231 per-priority sound responses are trials, not people.
Clinical introduction, calendar time, repeated testing and training covary with the alarm redesign; pre–post association does not isolate the acoustic redesign as a causal agent.
Main pooled recognizability interval includes 1; three priority-specific contrasts must not be transformed into an all-priority superiority claim.
Participants' perception that alarms were less distressing is not an observed patient stress or safety outcome.
MacBook playback was not formally calibrated for SPL/frequency response and test conditions are not identical to live operating-room events.
Author-reported numbers need R006 selection and R009 source-manifest/figure/supplement appraisal before quantitative incorporation.

source_routes.title: Improved pointer in auditory alarms enhances response accuracy
source_routes.reading_extent: PubMed indexed metadata and full abstract; selected publicly indexed PMC text excerpts describing Methods and Results; publisher fulltext request returned 403 in the web interface; no complete PDF or image-checked result figures
locators: PMC indexed excerpt > Results and response-time inclusion description

author_reported_not_independently_extrac.response_time_analysis_subset: Public indexed PMC methods excerpt reports 22/26 clinicians and 16/19 non-clinicians eligible for a response-time subset; verify source before any R009 numerical extraction

cautions: Controlled laboratory pointer manipulation, not real clinical implementation; cannot be pooled directly with the pre–post hospital redesign study.
Accuracy improvement in the specific pointer task is not evidence that any less-emotional or more-pleasant audio universally improves comprehension.
Only abstract and web-indexed fragments were consulted, not a hash-bound full paper; response-time subset must be independently checked.
Comparator is an earlier pointer design and does not establish participant reuse or independence relative to previous publications.

cross_source_interpretation.classification: hypothesis-generating contrast, not a meta-analysis, matched replication, or cross-paper pooled study
cross_source_interpretation.statement: One clinical pre/post investigation reports improved sound appeal with degraded low/medium-priority recognition; a different short laboratory pointer experiment reports improved accuracy. Effects depend on actual message/priority mapping, cue manipulation, task and evaluation context.
not_inferred: a measured benefit of emotionally neutral voice
